key_insight: Representations learned by independent foundation models for interatomic potentials converge to a common 'platonic' geometry, enabling direct cross-model comparison and arithmetic in embedding space without requiring ground-truth labels.
problem_solved: Different foundation models produce incompatible embeddings, making it hard to compare, combine, or diagnose models for interatomic potentials; the paper provides a unified geometric basis to align and evaluate them.
method: Compute atomic/structure embeddings from multiple independent foundation ML potentials for the same set of configurations.
Align and analyze these embeddings to reveal a shared low-dimensional 'platonic' geometry that is model-agnostic.
Demonstrate embedding arithmetic and develop ground-truth-free diagnostics based on geometric consistency across models.
impact: Enables model-agnostic benchmarking, interpretability, and transfer (e.g., arithmetic-based property inference) across different foundation potentials without requiring expensive ground-truth data. This streamlines model selection, combination, and reliability assessment in ML-driven materials and chemistry workflows.
visual_elements: Schematic: multiple models (icons) mapping the same atomic structure to embeddings that overlap into a shared 'platonic' manifold.
Scatter/UMAP plot: aligned embeddings from different models showing a common geometric shape and cluster correspondence.
Illustration of embedding arithmetic: vector addition/subtraction in the shared space producing meaningful atomic/structural transformations.
Flowchart: pipeline for ground-truth-free diagnostics — compute embeddings, align geometry, compute consistency metrics.
paper_title: Platonic representation of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials
